# A full-rank occupied lattice core survives one-cap section trimming

This exact example rules out a proposed higher-dimensional extension of
the one-integer endpoint-trimming argument based on ONE cap alone. It
does not provide a simultaneous covering menu, global deepestness at all
listed marks, or a counterexample to OC.

Let n=4,d=1 and set

    C={(z,x): z in [-2,2]^4,
                 -1<=x<=min(1,2-||z||_infinity)}.

The upper roof is the minimum of finitely many affine functions, hence
concave. Thus C is a compact full-dimensional convex body. Every sampled
fiber has positive length. The cap x>=0 has proper sections at the 81
integer bases I={-1,0,1}^4 and outside supporting sections at the other
544 integer bases J={-2,-1,0,1,2}^4 minus I. All section coareas equal 1.
Its mass is 81; the total mixed volume is 2*81+544=706.

The genuine section family is convex, and the global constant envelope
is D=[-1,1]. Equality holds on the whole real cube [-1,1]^4. In particular
it holds on the full-dimensional occupied crosspolytope

    B=conv{+e_i,-e_i:1<=i<=4},

whose interior contains the integer point zero.

Define the necessary outside-trimmed centroid region

    T={ [sum_(z in I) z + sum_(z in J) tau_z z]
          /[81+sum_(z in J) tau_z] : 0<=tau_z<=1 }.

For J_+={z in J:z_1>0}, direct integer sums give

    #J_+ = 2*5^3-1*3^3 =223,
    sum_(J_+) z_1 = (1+2)*5^3-1*3^3 =348,
    sum_(J_+) z_i =0, i=2,3,4.

Take tau_z=81/125 on J_+ and zero elsewhere. Since 348-223=125,

    (81/125)*348 /[81+(81/125)*223]=1.

This law has centroid e_1. Coordinate permutations and sign changes
give every +/-e_i. Taking all selectors zero gives centroid zero.
The region T is convex: mixing two unnormalized selector laws and
renormalizing gives any prescribed convex mixture of their centroids,
with selectors still in [0,1]. Consequently B is contained in T.

The same selectors certify genuine LOCAL base-tilt cap minimality at
the marks (p,0), p in {0,+/-e_i}. For sufficiently small a in R^4,
the exact cap mass through (p,0) is

    F_p(a)=81-81 a.p + sum_(z in J)[a.(z-p)]_+.

For the selector law with centroid p,

    sum_(z in J) tau_z(z-p)=81p.

Using [r]_+>=tau r pointwise gives F_p(a)>=81. All proper sections
remain proper in this neighborhood, and outside contributions have
not yet saturated, so this is the actual cap formula, not merely a
formal derivative. In d=1 the positive continuous-normal direction
has no additional orientation parameter after positive normalization.

Thus full source-envelope compatibility, exact sampled section
Brunn--Minkowski, every one-cap base-tilt inequality, and a
full-dimensional occupied lattice source core do not by themselves
contradict each other. A higher-n exclusion must use the simultaneous
covering menu or a stronger global condition.
